repository_function.signature: (X1: 'Sequence[Sequence[float]]', X2: 'Sequence[Sequence[float]]', alpha: 'float' = 0.05, clf: 'Any | None' = None, mode: 'str' = 'realizable', *, q_values: 'Sequence[int]' = (2, 4, 8, 16, 32), random_state: 'int' = 0) -> 'tuple[float, dict[str, Any]]'
repository_function.docstring_verbatim:
Estimate a rejection-generic lower bound on ``TV(P1, P2)``.

For a binary test with class-conditional errors e0 and e1,
``TV(P1,P2) >= 1 - e0 - e1``. The implementation
replaces each held-out error by a one-sided Clopper-Pearson upper limit and
maximizes the resulting lower bound over a Bonferroni-protected q ladder.
The ``realizable`` mode records the explicit assumption that the chosen
classifier family contains (or sufficiently approximates) a useful test;
the held-out confidence statement itself is conditional on the trained
classifier and does not make that assumption distribution-free.
repository_function.call_confirmation: The runner called tv_lower_bound_divisibility for every validity replication and every real pair-k row; no replacement implementation was used.

assumption_sentence: In mode="realizable", the selected classifier family is assumed to contain, or sufficiently approximate, a useful binary rejection test; the held-out confidence statement is conditional on the trained classifier and is not distribution-free.

pre_registered_validity.criterion: At alpha=0.05, across 120 independent synthetic replications (20 at each k in {5,10,15,20,25,30}), count a violation whenever the returned lower bound exceeds the analytically known true TV for that replication.
pre_registered_validity.split: 70% training / 30% held-out test, stratified; implemented by the repository function
pre_registered_validity.falsifies_if: The violation rate is greater than the declared alpha=0.05.
pre_registered_validity.truth: P is uniform on binary k-vectors; Q is a calibrated mixture with the all-ones vector, so true TV is known exactly.
pre_registered_validity.selection: This criterion and replication grid are fixed before the synthetic validity measurements and before real-data measurements.

object_and_channel.object_channel_statement: The measured object is the k-prefix symbol law: draw a flow from a service and map its first k masked (direction, size) symbols, using PPI[1] direction and PPI[2] size only; PPI[0] inter-packet timing is excluded; flows require PPI_LEN >= k.
object_and_channel.deviation: At headline M=1, size_bins_m1_all_zero was measured true, so X6 uses the equivalent binary direction bit-vector encoding and omits the constant size coordinate; this changes representation, not the channel law.
object_and_channel.reference_object_definition: The k-prefix SYMBOL law at k=5, M=1: draw a flow uniformly from a service and map its first five masked (direction, size) symbols to one of 32 categorical cells.

headline_k_cert.source: project headline context / ROADMAP entry; printed by this runner before completion

large_k_fraction.definition: large k means k >= 15; each k retains its own eligible pair denominator
large_k_fraction.interpretation: The per-k fractions are the citable pair fractions. The pooled values summarize pair-k evaluations and are not a unique-pair fraction. All large-k entries are EXPLORATORY because the plug-in upper side is lost.

headline_comparison.source: project headline context / ROADMAP entry; printed by this runner before completion

cache_and_cost.cost_basis: The run uses merged.pkl codes/lens, ledger.json, results.pkl, and 360 cached NPZ parts; no H5 read is needed because the M=1 channel's size coordinate is constant by the existing headline masking validation.
cache_and_cost.estimated_real_calls: one repository-function call per eligible service pair and k=5..30, with at most 20000 cached flows per service

sampling.service_pair_rule: Both services must have at least 2000 cached flows with PPI_LEN >= k.
sampling.sample_selection: Deterministic seeded without-replacement subsample from cached eligible flows when the cap binds; all eligible cached flows otherwise.
